subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats automatically provision per-sender subagents with isolated skills/config/memory, or should OpenClaw keep sender-scoped group sessions as the supported isolation model and track subagent/skill policy separately?
rationale: Current source shows partial session and subagent infrastructure, but the requested default behavior changes channel routing, agent lifecycle, memory isolation, skills, config writes, and security boundaries.

options.title: Keep as Feishu product design
options.body: Use this issue as the umbrella decision for whether Feishu should get automatic group sender subagents, then split any approved implementation into narrow API/plugin/security tasks.

options.title: Narrow to session-scope isolation
options.body: Treat `group_sender` and `group_topic_sender` as the supported current path and rewrite the per-user subagent parts as separate optional follow-up work.

options.title: Defer to adjacent API issues
options.body: Resolve Feishu account identity, channel subagent threading, and user-level skill preference contracts before revisiting automatic group subagents.

recommendation.title: Keep as Feishu product design
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the umbrella decision for whether Feishu should get automatic group sender subagents, then split any approved implementation into narrow API/plugin/security tasks.

likelyOwner.reason: They most directly own the current Feishu group routing, dynamic-agent, and subagent-hook code paths involved in this decision.
